source_note: Bank: 5 levels x 5 questions = 25. Level 3 is typed question-and-answer (no options). Levels 4 and 5 are slightly harder. Optional 'code' field renders as a code block.

questions.question: A corrupted location string has surfaced in the system. The characters appear scrambled, but no character has been changed. Sometimes, repairing corrupted data requires nothing more than changing your point of view.
questions.code: K C A B R O O D T N O R F

_answer.explanation: Reading the characters from right to left reveals FRONTDOORBACK.

questions.question:
The Logic Lock

Two binary signals guard the final lock. The system activates every bit that is switched on in either signal. Combine the two signals using a bitwise OR operation. What is the resulting binary code?

_answer.explanation: A bitwise OR produces 1 whenever either corresponding bit is 1. Applying OR to 10101100 and 11000011 produces 11101111.

questions.question: A web developer requests a resource that no longer exists at the specified location. The server returns a familiar three-digit response. Somewhere in this building, a physical room bears that same number. Identify the room and enter its number.

_answer.explanation: HTTP status code 404 means Not Found. The required room number is 404.

questions.question:
Encrypted System Log

The system records the following operations. After the sequence finishes, identify the card currently at the top of the stack.

_answer.explanation: PUSH adds an item to the top of the stack, while POP removes the top item. DOOR is pushed last, so the first POP removes DOOR and the second removes CLOCK. WINDOW remains at the top.

questions.question: An intercepted message appears to contain a hidden route. The analyst left behind a cryptic note: "You're closer than the letters suggest. The truth lies just before the message." Recover the original message.

_answer.explanation: Each letter has been shifted one position forward in the alphabet. Shift every letter one position backward to reveal THERE IS A SECRET PATH.

questions.title: The Missing Treasure
questions.question:
Mission: The treasure scanner skips the final item. Identify the bug to recover all four numbers.

Which change fixes the bug?
options: Change i = 0 to i = 1
Change i < 3 to i < 4
Change i++ to i--
Change treasure[] to treasure()

_answer.explanation: Array indices are 0, 1, 2, and 3. The condition i < 3 stops the loop before index 3, skipping 40. Changing it to i < 4 prints all four numbers.

questions.title: The Corrupted Treasure Decoder
questions.question:
Mission: The treasure decoder should combine scattered letters into the secret password, but a bug prevents it from working.

Find and fix the bug so that the program prints:
Secret password: VAULT

Enter the corrected line inside the loop.
questions.code:
letters = ["V", "A", "U", "L", "T"]
password = ""

for i in range(5):
    password = letters[i]

print("Secret password:", password)

_answer.explanation: The original line replaces the password with one letter during every iteration. Using += appends each letter to the existing password, producing VAULT.

questions.title: The Double Identity
questions.question: Identify the change needed to fix the error in this Python code.
options: Change the first line to x == 5
Change the if line to if x == 5:
Remove the if statement
Replace print with input

_answer.explanation: The single equals sign assigns a value, while == compares two values. The if statement must use == to check whether x equals 5.

questions.title: The Broken Tags
questions.question: What is the problem with the following HTML code?
options: The b tag cannot contain text
The inner i tag must close before the outer b tag
HTML does not support nested tags
Both tags must be replaced with p

_answer.explanation: Nested tags should close in the reverse order in which they were opened. The corrected code is Lost Archives.

questions.title: The Vanishing Variable
questions.question:
Mission: The vault refuses to open because the program refers to a variable that does not exist.

Identify the bug and enter ONLY the corrected line of code.

_answer.explanation: Python is case-sensitive. The variable is declared as vault_code, but the code tries to access vault_Code. The corrected line is print(vault_code).

questions.title: The Memory Keeper
questions.question: Riddle: I remember what you are working on, helping your computer access it quickly. But when the power goes out, my contents disappear. What am I?

_answer.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) temporarily stores data and instructions currently in use. It is volatile, so its contents are lost when power is removed.

questions.title: The Indented Trail
questions.question: Riddle: I use indentation to define blocks of code, and my name is also associated with a type of snake. Which programming language am I?

_answer.explanation: Python uses indentation to define code blocks, and its name is associated with the snake.

questions.title: The Invisible Bridge
questions.question: Riddle: I connect your device to a network without a physical cable. You often use me to access the internet at home, college, or a café. What am I?

_answer.explanation: Wi-Fi allows devices to connect to a network wirelessly.

questions.title: The Style Spell
questions.question: Riddle: HTML gives a webpage its structure, but I control its colours, fonts, spacing, and layout. What technology am I? Enter my abbreviation and full form.

_answer.explanation: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets. It controls the visual presentation of webpages.

questions.title: The Endless Journey
questions.question:
I repeat the same journey again and again.

I obey a condition, yet one mistake can trap me forever.

My exit is written in the code, but sometimes I never reach it.

What am I?

_answer.explanation: A loop repeats a block of code. If its stopping condition is never met, it can become an infinite loop.

questions.title: The Urgent Warning
questions.question:
Mission: You receive an email claiming your college account will be permanently deleted in 10 minutes unless you click a link and enter your password.

What is the strongest warning sign that this could be a phishing attempt?
options: The email contains a greeting
It uses urgency and pressure to make you reveal credentials
It mentions your college
It was sent during the day

_answer.explanation: Scammers often create panic and impose artificial deadlines to pressure people into revealing passwords or clicking malicious links.

questions.title: The Four Emails: Find the Impostor
questions.question: Mission: Four emails arrive in your inbox. Which one is most likely a phishing attempt?
options: library@svit.edu.in — Your reserved library book is ready for collection.
security@paypaI-support.example — Your account will be permanently blocked in 10 minutes. Click here to verify your password.
events@svit.edu.in — Your registration for the college fest is confirmed.
noreply@results.example — Your semester results are now available. Visit the official student portal.

_answer.explanation: Option B combines an urgent threat with a suspicious sender address. The name uses a capital I in place of the lowercase l in 'paypal', making it a potential lookalike. Never trust a sender based only on its display name.

questions.title: The QR Reward Trap
questions.question:
Mission: A stall displays a QR code promising you a ₹500 reward. After scanning it, the page asks for your UPI PIN to receive the money.

What should you do?
options: Enter the PIN if the page has the stall's logo
Enter the PIN and change it later
Do not enter the PIN; verify the offer through a trusted channel
Ask a friend to enter their PIN first

_answer.explanation: A UPI PIN authorizes payments; it is not needed to receive money. Never enter it on a suspicious page.

questions.title: The False Security Seal
questions.question:
Mission: A phishing website looks exactly like a legitimate banking website and uses HTTPS with a padlock icon in the browser.

Which statement is the most accurate?
options: The padlock proves that the website is genuine and safe.
HTTPS encrypts the connection, but it does not prove that the website itself is legitimate.
Phishing websites cannot use HTTPS certificates.
A website is safe as long as its URL begins with https://.

_answer.explanation: HTTPS encrypts data sent between your browser and the website, but scammers can also obtain HTTPS certificates. Always verify the domain and use trusted links.

questions.title: The Disguised Result
questions.question:
Mission: You receive an email from your college's usual-looking address. It has the correct logo, your full name, and perfect grammar. It asks you to open an attachment called Exam_Results.pdf.exe.

What should you conclude?
options: It is legitimate because the logo is correct.
It is safe because the sender address looks familiar.
It is suspicious because the .exe extension indicates an executable file; verify with the college before opening it.
It is safe if antivirus is installed.

_answer.explanation: The final extension is .exe, indicating an executable file. A convincing logo, familiar-looking sender, and perfect grammar do not guarantee safety. Verify the attachment with the college through a trusted channel.

questions.title: The Bitwise Key
questions.question:
Mission: Two binary keys must be combined using bitwise OR to reveal the next code.

Enter the resulting 8-bit binary number.

_answer.explanation: Bitwise OR gives 1 whenever either corresponding bit is 1. The resulting binary number is 11111110.

questions.title: The Final Combination
questions.question:
Mission: Evaluate the logic circuit to unlock the final combination.

A = 1
B = 1
C = 0
X = (A AND B) OR C

What is the value of X?
options: Cannot be determined

_answer.explanation: First, A AND B = 1 AND 1 = 1. Then 1 OR 0 = 1. Therefore, X = 1.

questions.title: The Universal Key
questions.question:
In the world of digital logic, one gate holds a special power: by combining multiple copies of itself, you can construct every other basic logic gate. Its output is LOW only when both inputs are HIGH.

Question: Which logic gate possesses this universal property?
options: AND
OR
NAND
XOR

_answer.explanation: NAND is a universal logic gate. Its output is LOW only when both inputs are HIGH, and NAND gates alone can be combined to construct other basic logic gates.

questions.title: The NOR Secret
questions.question: In digital electronics, which statement about a NOR gate is correct?
options: It produces HIGH when at least one input is HIGH.
It produces HIGH only when all inputs are HIGH.
It produces HIGH only when all inputs are LOW.
It always produces the opposite output of an XOR gate.

_answer.explanation: A NOR gate is the opposite of an OR gate. It produces HIGH only when all its inputs are LOW.

questions.title: Will the Alarm Go Off?
questions.question:
Boolean Logic Challenge: A high-security vault uses this logic circuit:

Y = NOT (A AND B) AND C

Given:
A = 1
B = 1
C = 0

What happens when the circuit evaluates the inputs?
options: The alarm goes off
The alarm stays silent
The vault self-destructs
The system enters lockdown

_answer.explanation: First, A AND B = 1. NOT 1 = 0. Then 0 AND C (which is 0) = 0. The output is LOW, so the alarm stays silent.
